paragraphs.en: Let's take a minute to think about how {precious} water is.It forms an important part of the earth's {atmosphere} , and the human body is 60% water.When we are {thirsty} , we will fill a {glass} with clean water.Without water, even simple tasks like using the {washroom} or preparing meals would become challenging.Furthermore, water is essential to not only humans, but also to other species such as {dolphins} and {frogs} that rely on clean water for survival.
paragraphs.cn: 让我们花一分钟时间思考水有多 <u> 宝贵 </u> 。水构成了地球 <u> 大气 </u> 层的重要组成部分，而人体中60%都是水。当我们感到 <u> 口渴 </u> 时，会倒一 <u> 杯 </u> 干净的水来解渴。没有水的话，即使像使用 <u> 洗手间 </u> 或准备饭菜这样简单的活动也会变得困难重重。此外，水不仅对人类至关重要，对于其他像 <u> 海豚 </u> 和 <u> 青蛙 </u> 这样依赖清洁水源生存的物种来说也是如此。

paragraphs.en: We use water {indirectly} too.For example, {farmers} use water to make the plants grow.Without {sufficient} water, plants may dry out.Many {factories} also use water during the production of {clothing} , textiles ( (纺织品) ) and so on.
paragraphs.cn: 我们还会 <u> 间接地 </u> 使用水。例如， <u> 农民 </u> 利用水来促使植物生长。没有 <u> 足够的 </u> 水分，植物可能会枯萎。许多 <u> 工厂 </u> 在生产 <u> 服装 </u> 、纺织品等制品的过程中也要用到水。

paragraphs.en: The {truth} is that we are {lucky} enough to have clean water whenever we want, but this is not the case for many people around the world.The lack of water can lead to {severe crises} such as {drought} .This is a significant concern worldwide, especially in {Africa} . {Rivers} and lakes are drying up, causing a {decrease} in water {supply} for both drinking and farming.
paragraphs.cn: <u> 事实 </u> 是，我们足够 <u> 幸运 </u> ，能够随时获得干净的水，但对于世界上的许多人来说，情况并非如此。水资源短缺可能会引发 <u> 严重的危机 </u> ，比如 <u> 干旱 </u> 。这是全球性的重大问题，特别是在 <u> 非洲 </u> 。 <u> 河流 </u> 和湖泊正在干涸，导致饮用水和农业灌溉用水的 <u> 供应量减少 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: {Pollution} is another major problem that causes the {shortage} of clean water.Waste materials dumped ( (倾倒) ) into rivers and the {ocean} pose a {threat} to both the environment and public health.If we drink dirty water, we can catch diseases and become {ill} .Every year over 500,000 children die from diarrhea ( (腹泻) ) caused by dirty water.Also, in some countries, children walk many {kilometers} every day to get water.If children spend hours each day collecting water, they can't go to school for an education.
paragraphs.cn: <u> 污染 </u> 是导致清洁用水 <u> 短缺 </u> 的另一个主要问题。倾倒进河流和 <u> 海洋 </u> 中的废料对环境和公众健康都构成了 <u> 威胁 </u> 。如果我们引用不干净的水，就可能感染疾病，身体 <u> 不适 </u> 。每年有超过50万名儿童因饮用不干净的水而死于腹泻。此外，在一些国家，孩子们每天需要走好几 <u> 公里 </u> 去取水。如果孩子们每天要花费数小时去取水，那他们就无法上学接受教育了。

paragraphs.en: {Economic} support and proper planning can help supply safe water to those in need.In 1993 the United Nations decided that March 22nd would be World Water Day.During this {annual} event, countries around the world {hold} activities to {educate} people about water issues.It provides an opportunity to {advocate} for innovative {solutions} for water management.Schools organize {campaigns} to promote water conservation.They make {posters} and hold {competitions} to encourage inventions for solving water shortages.Some students take {trips} to the local {beach} to collect {rubbish} and clean up the {sea} .At one school in the UK, children walk 6 km with 6 {liters} of water.In this way, they know how it feels to walk a long distance carrying heavy bottles.
paragraphs.cn: <u> 经济上的 </u> 支持和合理的规划有助于为有需要的人提供安全的饮用水。1993年，联合国将3月22日定为“世界水日”。在这个 <u> 一年一度的 </u> 活动期间，世界各国都会 <u> 举办 </u> 活动，就水资源问题进行科普 <u> 教育 </u> 。这为 <u> 倡导 </u> 创新的水资源管理 <u> 解决方案 </u> 提供了契机。各个学校会组织开展节约用水的宣传 <u> 运动 </u> 。他们制作 <u> 海报 </u> ，举办 <u> 竞赛 </u> ，以鼓励人们发明出解决水资源短缺问题的方案。一些学生会 <u> 前往 </u> 当地的 <u> 海滩 </u> 收集 <u> 垃圾 </u> 并清理 <u> 海洋 </u> 。在英国的一所学校，孩子们携带6 <u> 升 </u> 水步行6公里。通过这种方式，他们可以体会到背着沉重的水瓶长途步行是什么样的感觉。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
